question: Which celebration in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana signifies the start of the harvest season and the official start of the New Year?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ugadi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

 
• **Ugadi** is the **New Year celebration** primarily observed in the Indian states of **Andhra Pradesh**, **Telangana**, and **Karnataka**. It marks the beginning of the **Chaitra month** of the Hindu lunisolar calendar.
 
• The festival signifies the **start of the harvest season** and celebrates the onset of spring. It is considered an auspicious time for new beginnings.
 
• The word "Ugadi" is derived from the Sanskrit words **"Yuga" (age)** and **"Adi" (beginning)**, meaning the **beginning of a new age**.
 
• Ugadi is celebrated with traditional rituals, including cleaning homes, decorating entrances with **mango leaves** and **rangoli**, and preparing a special dish known as **Ugadi Pachadi**, which symbolizes the different flavors of life.
